title: Developmental Psychology Adventure 3: Erikson & Identity

concepts.def: Erikson — social conflicts at each age

walkthroughs.body_html:
Erik Erikson (1950) extended Freud across the lifespan.

1. Trust vs mistrust (0–1).
2. Autonomy vs shame (1–3).
3. Initiative vs guilt (3–6).
4. Industry vs inferiority (6–12).
5. Identity vs role confusion (12–18).
6. Intimacy vs isolation (young adult).
7. Generativity vs stagnation (mid).
8. Integrity vs despair (late).

Stage 5 — adolescence — is the spotlight stage.

James Marcia (1966) refined it into four identity statuses: diffusion, foreclosure, moratorium, achievement.

Crisis (exploration) × commitment defines each status. Healthy outcome: identity achievement after moratorium.

Erikson highlighted that development continues across life — a major advance over Freud.

Limits: hard to test; ages are approximate; based on Western, individualist samples; later stages may not generalise to collectivist cultures.
